name: Jessie Ware
label: EMI / Interscope
lede: A Clapham journalist and backing singer becomes a Mercury-shortlisted pop star, nearly quits after her third album, and turns it around with a podcast with her mum and a disco record.

eras.title: Backing vocals and a heart-shaped record
eras.text: Before any solo record, Jessie Ware is a journalist, a TV researcher and a touring backing singer. Two dance-world introductions, SBTRKT and Sampha, turn her into the voice people in London are asking about.

years.h: A Jewish Chronicle desk, a Daily Mirror sports desk, then a van
years.p: After Sussex, Ware worked at the Jewish Chronicle, the Daily Mirror and the TV company Love Productions, and sang backing vocals on tour for [[Jack Peñate|9b64cf5d-1f4a-45b5-a84a-5109a88f178f]], including in the US.
years.xp:
Ware grew up in Clapham and went to Alleyn's School in Dulwich, where Florence Welch, Jack Peñate and Felix White of the Maccabees were schoolmates. She studied English literature at the University of Sussex.

Peñate's tour is where she learned to be a front person from the side of the stage. She has credited it as training for her solo career.

years.h: [[SBTRKT|7f2aa196-cfd4-4a3d-ace3-28b7b6a79af7]] gets her on "Nervous"
years.p: Introduced through Peñate's bandmate Tic, Ware sang on SBTRKT's "Nervous" for PMR, the first record with her voice on it that got noticed.
years.xp: The PMR connection led to "The Vision", a collaboration with the DJ Joker, which Wikipedia says helped seal her own deal with the label.

years.h: "Valentine" with [[Sampha|130c2184-14f2-4180-a216-04b5a333be57]], on heart-shaped vinyl
years.p: Ware met Sampha through SBTRKT, and Young Turks pressed their duet "Valentine" on a heart-shaped record.
years.xp: Wikipedia says the song was partly inspired by a James Blake track and by the couple's own romantic experiences. Ware also sang on Florence and the Machine's 2011 album Ceremonials, for a school friend.

years.h: "Strangest Feeling": purple 10-inch, no chart
years.p: Her first solo single came out on limited purple 10-inch vinyl through PMR and did not chart on the UK Singles Chart.

eras.title: Devotion and a Mercury nod
eras.text: Devotion makes her a name in the UK, lands on the Mercury list, and travels to the US with a rapper's verse attached. She spends 2013 touring it.

years.h: "Running" is the first single off Devotion
years.p: The lead single came out six months before Devotion, on Ware's own PMR and Island deal.

years.h: Devotion, made with the Invisible's [[Dave Okumu|abb29383-f013-479d-bf75-1cd57c9b95ed]]
years.p: Okumu produced twelve of the fourteen original tracks. It debuted at No. 5 in the UK and went on to UK Gold certification.
years.xp:
The Guardian called it poised and restrained, writing that dance music "clearly runs through" the vocalist's veins. The album's Metacritic score is 85 from 28 reviews. Pitchfork later put it on its list of the 100 best albums of 2010 to 2014.

One song had a name change: "110%" was first titled "If You're Never Gonna Move" after sample clearance disputes over a Big Pun interpolation.

years.h: First Mercury Prize nomination
years.p: Devotion made the shortlist for the Mercury Prize for Album of the Year, alongside MOBO and Brit nominations in the female and breakthrough categories.

years.h: US release on Interscope, with a verse from A$AP Rocky
years.p: Devotion reached the US on April 16 via Cherrytree and Interscope; the Gold Edition added four tracks and a "Wildest Moments" remix with A$AP Rocky.
years.xp: Wikipedia says Ware was promoting in the States and Rocky's verses arrived just before the deadline. The US Billboard 200 peak was No. 79.

eras.title: Major-label polish, then a baby
eras.text: Tough Love goes bigger and more pop, with her best-known single. Then a two-year break from performing, a baby in 2016 and an album she isn't happy with.

years.src: Wikipedia: Tough Love (Jessie Ware album) · Wikipedia: Jessie Ware
years.h: Tough Love: Dev Hynes, Miguel, BenZel
years.p: Her second album reached No. 9 in the UK and went Gold; the title track was her first UK top-40 single at No. 34.
years.xp:
Wikipedia and Ware's own page disagree on the UK release date: October 6 and October 13. Metacritic has it at 74 from 26 reviews. Pitchfork wrote that "rarely does a major-label pop singer sound as tasteful as Ware does."

Ware also sang the chorus on "The Crying Game" for Nicki Minaj's 2014 album The Pinkprint.

years.src: Double J: Ten years in, Jessie Ware is enjoying her career more than ever · Wikipedia: Tough Love (Jessie Ware album)
years.h: "Say You Love Me", written with Ed Sheeran in Benny Blanco's bedroom
years.p: Ware co-wrote the song with [[Ed Sheeran|b8a7c51f-362c-4dcb-a259-bc6e0095f0a6]] and [[Benny Blanco|5a6131f9-f8db-4722-b4d7-6a0c7183c590]] and it became her biggest UK hit, at No. 22.
years.xp: Ware told Double J it was one of her proudest moments, writing it "with Ed in Benny's tiny bedroom studio in New York." Ware later co-wrote "New Man" on Sheeran's 2017 album ÷ and sang backing vocals on it.

years.h: The Roundhouse, iTunes Festival
years.p: Filmed at the iTunes Festival in London, a live "Wildest Moments" from the Tough Love tour year, filmed at the Roundhouse in London.

years.h: Benny Blanco hears the album and says start again
years.p: After a rushed first pass at her third album, Blanco told Ware in December 2016 the material was really shit, according to Wikipedia's account.
years.xp:
Ware had rushed to finish the record before her baby arrived in September 2016 and wasn't satisfied. Blanco asked why she wasn't making the music she actually wanted to.

She rebuilt the album with new sessions, including with Starsmith and James Newman, and named Childish Gambino's Awaken, My Love!, Solange's A Seat at the Table and Christine and the Queens as reference points.

eras.title: The low point and the podcast
eras.text: Glasshouse lands softly and Ware seriously considers ending her music career. A podcast with her mother gives her a different job, and a new label and management give her a different record.

years.h: Glasshouse, named after an Edward Thomas poem
years.p: Her third album entered the UK chart at No. 7 with 8,448 units, her third straight top-ten debut, and got mixed-to-good reviews.
years.xp:
Metacritic averaged 72 from 13 reviews. AllMusic noted "finely woven adult-pop ballads" but a "stitched-together quality"; Clash found it too safe. The cover is Ware at Neuendorf House in Mallorca, a 1991 modernist villa by John Pawson and Claudio Silvestrin.

Collaborators included Benny Blanco, Ed Sheeran, Julia Michaels, Cashmere Cat, Kid Harpoon and Francis and the Lights.

years.cap: Performance of Jessie Ware in the Islington Assembly Hall in September 2017. · Wikimedia
years.src: Table Manners: About · Wikipedia: Jessie Ware
years.h: Table Manners starts, and [[Sam Smith|5a85c140-dcf9-4dd2-b2c8-aff0471549f3]] is guest one
years.p: Jessie and her mother Lennie launch a podcast for Acast and Island Records in which famous people eat dinner at their table.
years.xp:
The show has run for 18 series and more than 200 episodes, and its own site claims over 60 million downloads. It won Best New Voice at the 2018 Audio Production Awards and Best Podcast at the 2022 NME Awards.

Guests have included Ed Sheeran, Nigella Lawson, Daniel Kaluuya, Paul McCartney and Kylie Minogue. A cookbook followed in 2020.

years.big: "I'd had a child and was trying to show everybody I could be everything."
q: I'd had a child and was trying to show everybody I could be everything.
years.src: Double J: Ten years in, Jessie Ware is enjoying her career more than ever · Music Week: The Music Week Interview: Jessie Ware · Wikipedia: What's Your Pleasure?
years.h: She thinks her music career might be over
years.p: Ware told Double J that Glasshouse left her feeling her career was going to finish, and she considered leaving music.
years.xp: She has said the podcast made her more comfortable in her skin and let her talk about her life without pressure to put it all into songs. Music Week's 2023 profile names her new management, Fascination (Peter Loraine and Sarah Jackson), and Universal UK chairman David Joseph as people who pushed her toward a change of label.

years.h: "Adore You" is the first sign of the new sound
years.p: The single came in February 2019, first of the run that became What's Your Pleasure?, and it opened the disco era.

eras.title: What's Your Pleasure?
eras.text: A record made with James Ford that she treats as a party she can't throw in a pandemic. It is her highest-charting album to date and the turn the rest of her story runs on.

years.src: Wikipedia: What's Your Pleasure? · Music Week: The Music Week Interview: Jessie Ware
years.h: What's Your Pleasure? goes to No. 3 in lockdown
years.p: Pushed back twice by COVID and Juneteenth, the disco album became her first UK top-three entry; Pitchfork gave it 8.3 and Best New Music.
years.xp:
The first date was June 5, then June 19, then June 26. Ford co-produced and co-wrote; Metacritic has it at 84 from 18 reviews. Ware described it as a two-year labour of love about escapism.

Music Week's profile puts its sales at 66,426, below Devotion's 140,486, though it peaked higher on the chart.

years.h: The Platinum Pleasure Edition adds seven songs
years.p: The reissue added "Overtime", "Please", "Hot N Heavy" and an "Adore You" remix, in grayscale metallic packaging.

years.cap: Jessie Ware performing live at Space 15 Twenty in Hollywood, Los Angeles, California, on Sunday, November 5, 2017. · Wikimedia
years.src: Wikipedia: Kiss of Life (Kylie Minogue and Jessie Ware song)
years.h: "Kiss of Life" with Kylie Minogue
years.p: Ware joked she had bullied [[Kylie Minogue|2fddb92d-24b2-46a5-bf28-3aed46f4684c]] into a duet after Minogue's September 2020 Table Manners appearance; Ford produced.
years.xp: The song is on the reissue Disco: Guest List Edition; Minogue sang her part remotely from Melbourne. Sophie Muller shot the video at London's Ave Mario restaurant, inspired by Pedro Almodovar and 1980s telenovelas, with Ware as restaurateur and Minogue as food critic.

eras.title: Free Yourself
eras.text: The disco record's sequel is louder, funnier and built for crowds. A Glastonbury headline slot opens it, and Pitchfork, the Guardian and the Mercury list all notice.

years.cap: Jessie Ware performing live at Space 15 Twenty in Hollywood, Los Angeles, California, on Sunday, November 5, 2017. · Wikimedia
years.src: Wikipedia: Free Yourself (Jessie Ware song) · Music Week: The Music Week Interview: Jessie Ware
years.h: "Free Yourself" debuts on the Park stage at Glastonbury
years.p: Ware played the new song during her headline set on Glastonbury's Park stage, and it was released as a single on July 19.
years.xp: Stuart Price produced; Ware, Price and Clarence Coffee Jr. wrote it. Pitchfork put it at No. 49 on its year-end songs list, and Billboard at No. 33. Music Week's 2023 profile says she had supported Harry Styles and headlined the Park stage.

years.h: Ruby red dress, stately home, and a pinch of the occult
years.p: Vicky Lawton directed the "Free Yourself" video; Lawton called it "very '70s rock 'n' roll" with a touch of the occult.

years.src: Wikipedia: That! Feels Good! · Album of the Year: Jessie Ware, That! Feels Good! reviews · Under the Radar: Jessie Ware, That! Feels Good! review
years.h: That! Feels Good!: Pitchfork gives it 8.3, ranks it No. 22
years.p: Ware's fifth album reached No. 3 in the UK; Pitchfork's review scored it 8.3 and put it at No. 22 of the year.
years.xp:
Julianne Escobedo Shepherd wrote the Pitchfork review; per Wikipedia it calls the album "a genre revival album that's painstakingly true to its source material, but doesn't sound like a curdled rehash." Metacritic has 89; NME, the Guardian and the Financial Times gave five stars.

Stuart Price and James Ford produced, and Ware co-wrote with Shungudzo, Danny Parker, Clarence Coffee Jr. and Sarah Hudson. The title track opens with spoken cameos from Kylie Minogue, Gemma Arterton and Roisin Murphy. Rolling Stone put it at No. 18 and NME at No. 20 on year-end lists; PopMatters ranked it No. 1 of pop albums.

years.h: "Freak Me Now" brings in [[Roisin Murphy|4c56405d-ba8e-4283-99c3-1dc95bdd50e7]]
years.p: Ware's fourth single from the album featured Murphy, who also has a spoken cameo in the title track.

years.h: A second Mercury Prize shortlisting
years.p: That! Feels Good! was shortlisted for the Mercury Prize, her first nomination since Devotion in 2012.

eras.title: Superbloom
eras.text: A sixth album that keeps the dance floor but tries for more grown-up intimacy, with her first arena tour ahead.

years.h: Superbloom debuts at No. 2 in the UK
years.p: Her highest-charting album came out on EMI, with production from Ford, Price and Xenomania's Miranda Cooper and Jon Shave on the lead single.
years.xp:
Reviews were generally favorable: Metacritic 76. The Guardian felt it failed to deliver the jolt of What's Your Pleasure?, and Paste found it less fresh. Ware acts as her own A&R, as she has since 2020.

The Superbloom Tour, her first arena run, starts October 6, 2026 in Toronto and finishes December 5 in Manchester.
